Ok I am going to be trimming this down for publication and organizing in a way that matches exactly what is being asked of me in the manuscript

JULY 16 NOTE: none of this data is normal, so using lm stands to be a bit erroneous. I have done qq plots with log transformed data and it fits a lot better!

Also, for the question of AGE EFFECTS , I am going to remove ceramics and NHL-MgSr from the dataframe. Both of these were only sampled at 6 months, so are incomplete. 


```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = TRUE)
```

```{r loading packages}
library(tidyverse) #most things pipey
library(vegan) #pcoa plots
library(ape) #pcoa function

library(broom)
library(dplyr) #most things pipey
library(rstatix) #dunns

#for random forest

```

```{r reading in data}
setwd("/Users/enixon96/Desktop/DATABASE/2023/CUR23/SKELLY")

skelly <- read.csv("SKELLYlongFormat.csv")%>%
  mutate(timepoint = case_when(time.point == "1 week" ~ "1w",
                               time.point == "1 month" ~ "1mo",
                               time.point == "6 months" ~ "6mo",
                               TRUE ~ time.point),
         .keep = "unused")

```

setting up relevant dataframe
```{r setting up dataframes for age and substrate tests}
cnatDf <- skelly %>%
  filter(species == "Cnat") %>%
  #removing ceramics from analysis because it is not the focus?
  filter(substrate.type != "Ceramic" & substrate.type != "NHL-MgSr")%>%
  #removing missing NHL-Mg
  drop_na()
  #adding index for uniqueIDs

```

#random forest and PC1 analysis

random forest to identify the metrics that are the most informative for substrate type effects
```{r random forest - choosing predictor variables for growth metric }
#ok but area.volume is just a combo of area and volume so not sure if i should keep it

rf_all <- cnatDf%>%
  #removing the one missing NHL-Mg
  drop_na()%>%
  #select scaled variables and useful info only
  select(substrate.type, volume , area.volume, #timepoint,
         area,
         coralliteHeight ,
         septathickness,
         diameter)

# Make sure response is a factor
rf_all$substrate.type <- factor(rf_all$substrate.type)

# Check sample sizes
table(rf_all$substrate.type)

# Leave-one-out cross validation
ctrl <- trainControl(
  method = "LOOCV",
  classProbs = TRUE
)

set.seed(123)

#need to remove hyphens
levels(rf_all$substrate.type) <- make.names(levels(rf_all$substrate.type))

rf_model <- train(
  substrate.type ~ .,
  data = rf_all,
  method = "ranger",
  trControl = ctrl,
  importance = "permutation",
  num.trees = 1000
)

# Model summary
rf_model

# Variable importance
varImp(rf_model)

# Plot variable importance
plot(varImp(rf_model), main = "Variable Importance")


```

PCA using the top 3 metrics of interest
```{r PCA df set up}
cnat_pcaDf <- cnatDf%>%
#making uniqueIDs
  group_by(substrate.type, timepoint) %>%
  mutate(replicate = row_number()) %>%
  ungroup()%>%
  unite(sampleID, c(substrate.type, timepoint, replicate), sep = "_", remove = FALSE)%>%
#log transforming all values
  mutate(across(c(volume, area, area.volume, coralliteHeight, septathickness, diameter),log10,
                .names = "{.col}_log"))%>%
#selecting smapleID and log-transf growth variables
  select(2, 15:20)

```

data viz and PC analysis set up
```{r PCA top 3 area.volume_log septathickness_log diameter_log}

cnat_PCAdf_top3 <- cnat_pcaDf %>%
  select(sampleID, area.volume_log, septathickness_log, diameter_log)

cnat_PCA_top3 <- cnat_PCAdf_top3 %>%
  column_to_rownames(var = "sampleID") %>%
  #scale() %>%
  rda(scale = TRUE)

PC_df <- scores(cnat_PCA_top3, display = "sites") %>%
  as.data.frame() %>%
  rownames_to_column("sampleID")%>%
  mutate(PC1 = -PC1)

cnat_PCA_top3Plot <- PC_df %>%
  separate(sampleID, c("substrate.type", "timepoint", "replicate"), sep = "_")%>%
  ggplot(aes(x = PC1, y = PC2)) +
  geom_point(
    aes(color = substrate.type, shape = timepoint),size = 3)

cnat_PCA_top3Plot
```

cnaBiplot <- ggplot(site_scores, aes(PC1, PC2)) +

#linear models with log transformation

oct26 final note -ultimately i have chosen to log transform the data , which normalizes it pretty well and allows us to run a traditional anova. This I then follow up with a few iteractions of post hocs

post hoc 1 - dunnetts test to look for substrate differences within each timepoint

post hoc 2 - dunnetts test to look for substrate differences avging timepoint

post hoc 3 - tukey test to look for timepoint differences averaging across substrate types


I use the stats for the additive model because this is the best test for the question at hand, but I have to use the interactive model to do the dunnetts post hoc sectioned by timepoint. 

After all tests, I run a pval correction for all anova tests (5 tests x 2 factors = 10 tests). post hoc tests do not need to be included in this correction because corrections are made within each post hoc.

summary(cnatArea_int)

#MULTIPLE TEST P VALUE CORRECTION
```{r - corrections for all groeth var tests}
#but i need to correct for thew number of tests here so 
library(car)


pvals <- c(
  Anova(cnatVol_add, type = 2)["timepoint","Pr(>F)"],
  Anova(cnatVol_add, type = 2)["substrate.type","Pr(>F)"],

 
  Anova(cnatArea_add, type = 2)["timepoint","Pr(>F)"],
  Anova(cnatArea_add, type = 2)["substrate.type","Pr(>F)"],
  
  #Anova(cnatAreaVol_add, type = 2)["timepoint","Pr(>F)"],
  #Anova(cnatAreaVol_add, type = 2)["substrate.type","Pr(>F)"],
 
  Anova(cnatHeight_add, type = 2)["timepoint","Pr(>F)"],
  Anova(cnatHeight_add, type = 2)["substrate.type","Pr(>F)"],
 
  Anova(cnatThick_add, type = 2)["timepoint","Pr(>F)"],
  Anova(cnatThick_add, type = 2)["substrate.type","Pr(>F)"],

  Anova(cnatDiam_add, type = 2)["timepoint","Pr(>F)"],
  Anova(cnatDiam_add, type = 2)["substrate.type","Pr(>F)"]

)

adjust <- p.adjust(pvals, method="BH")

```

#CORRECTING FOR ALL TESTS
```{r - p value corrections}
#timepoint 
p_timepoint <- c(
  volume    = Anova(cnatVol_add,    type = 2)["timepoint", "Pr(>F)"],
  area      = Anova(cnatArea_add,   type = 2)["timepoint", "Pr(>F)"],
  height    = Anova(cnatHeight_add, type = 2)["timepoint", "Pr(>F)"],
  thickness = Anova(cnatThick_add,  type = 2)["timepoint", "Pr(>F)"],
  diameter  = Anova(cnatDiam_add,   type = 2)["timepoint", "Pr(>F)"]
)

p_timepoint_BH <- p.adjust(p_timepoint, method = "BH")

#substr
p_substrate <- c(
  volume    = Anova(cnatVol_add,    type = 2)["substrate.type", "Pr(>F)"],
  area      = Anova(cnatArea_add,   type = 2)["substrate.type", "Pr(>F)"],
  height    = Anova(cnatHeight_add, type = 2)["substrate.type", "Pr(>F)"],
  thickness = Anova(cnatThick_add,  type = 2)["substrate.type", "Pr(>F)"],
  diameter  = Anova(cnatDiam_add,   type = 2)["substrate.type", "Pr(>F)"]
)

p_substrate_BH <- p.adjust(p_substrate, method = "BH")

# results
LM_pvalCorrections <- data.frame(
  variable = names(p_timepoint),
  p_timepoint = p_timepoint,
  p_timepoint_BH = p_timepoint_BH,
  p_substrate = p_substrate,
  p_substrate_BH = p_substrate_BH
)

LM_pvalCorrections
```
